title: Control gallery
description: Every control this build can draw, with the schema that selects it. Use `schemaui web --schema examples/controls-gallery.schema.json` and compare each card against its `x-control` below.

text_inputs.title: Text
text_inputs.description: Strings, with and without an explicit control.

plain.title: Single line
plain.description: No hint at all: a string falls back to a text input.

explicit_text.title: Single line, explicit
explicit_text.description: `x-control: "text"` states what the fallback already picks. Useful when a hint elsewhere on the node would otherwise change it.

legacy_notes.title: Multi-line, legacy hint
legacy_notes.description: `x-multiline: true` is the older spelling of the same thing and still works.

numbers.title: Numbers
numbers.description: Numbers without a slider, to show that bounds alone do not change the control. Note that a control the schema asks for but that cannot render the value is a load error with a pointer, not a silent downgrade — so a refusal cannot be demonstrated in a file that has to load.

unbounded.title: Plain number
unbounded.description: A number with no bounds at all.

bounded_but_plain.title: Bounded, still plain
bounded_but_plain.description: `minimum`/`maximum` are validation keywords first. Without `x-control` this stays a number box — bounds do not imply a slider.

constrained.title: Bounded and stepped
constrained.description: `multipleOf` is read as the step, but only a `slider`/`range` has a track to apply it to. Here it constrains validation and nothing more.

sliders.title: Sliders
sliders.description: One handle. Needs `minimum` and `maximum`, because a track with one end would mean inventing the other.

replicas.title: Integer slider
replicas.description: An integer steps by whole units by default, so the slider only offers values the schema accepts.

timeout_seconds.title: Stepped slider
timeout_seconds.description: `multipleOf` becomes the step, so this moves in 15-second jumps.

sample_rate.title: Fractional slider
sample_rate.description: A `number` with no `multipleOf` gets a step that divides the span into about a hundred stops: 0.01 here, not a whole unit that would leave two positions.

log_level.title: Slider with marks
log_level.description: `x-slider-marks` takes bare numbers when the values speak for themselves.

scale.title: Slider with labelled marks
scale.description: Or `{"value": n, "label": "text"}` when they do not.

opacity.title: Percentage slider
opacity.description: Marks may carry their own unit in the label.

ranges.title: Ranges
ranges.description: Two handles. The value is an array of exactly two numbers, so `minItems` and `maxItems` are both required — the parser rejects a `range` without them. `minimum`/`maximum` sit on the array itself, which is where the track reads its ends from.

business_hours.title: Hour range
business_hours.description: An integer interval, stepped by whole hours.

bandwidth.title: Range with marks
bandwidth.description: `x-slider-marks` works the same way on a range as on a slider.

confidence.title: Fractional range
confidence.description: A `number` interval, so the step is derived.

choices.title: Choices
choices.description: Every enum control needs an `enum`; the difference between them is only how many options there are and how much room they need.

region.title: Select
region.description: The default for an enum, and the only one that stays tidy with a long list.

strategy.title: Segmented control
strategy.description: `x-control: "segmented"` — for a handful of short options, where seeing them all beats opening a dropdown.

tier.title: Radio group
tier.description: `x-control: "radio"` — stacked instead of inline, so each option has room for a longer label.

priority.title: Integer enum, segmented
priority.description: The enum values may be numbers; they are rendered by their labels.

verbose.title: Switch
verbose.description: The default for a boolean, and the right control when the change takes effect immediately.

enabled.title: Checkbox
enabled.description: `x-control: "checkbox"` — the same value, but it reads as part of a set of things being chosen rather than as an on/off switch.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Colour values. The picker is drawn by the UI, not by the browser's native colour input.

accent.title: Accent colour
accent.description: `x-control: "color"` on a string. The value is stored as a hex string.

background.title: Background colour
background.description: `format: "color"` alone is not enough — it is documentation, not a rendering instruction. Without `x-control` this stays a text input, which is deliberate: a schema can carry a format this build has no picker for.

conditional.title: Conditional
conditional.description: `x-visible-when` composes with any control: the field appears only while a sibling matches.

mode.title: Delivery mode
mode.description: Pick "scheduled" to reveal the window below.
